Giwa was charged to the court over allegation of forgery. The Police had accused Giwa of forging the letterhead paper of a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), Chief Awa Kalu.
But Kalu, in a letter to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Mr Kayode Egebtokun, put a lie to the allegation of the Police against Ibitade and Giwa.
Despite the letter of Prof Awa Kalu to the IGP, formally distancing himself from the allegation of forgery and impersonation against Giwa and Ibitade, the Police went ahead to press charge against Giwa.
Chief Kalu, in a letter to the IGP had said his letterhead was never forged and that he had not at any time lodged any complaint to the Police about forgery of his document.
Professor Kalu, in a letter dated May 30, 2025, addressed to the IGP, clarified that he neither filed a complaint nor reported Mr Giwa for allegedly forging his firm’s letterhead.
At the resumed trial, Dr Sonny Ajala (SAN), counsel to Awa Kalu (SAN), the subpoenaed non-party witness moved a motion to set aside the subpoena issued against Prof Kalu to appear before the court.
But the prosecutor S. A. Medugu Esq. applied for an arrest warrant to be issued against the Senior Advocate.
The first defendant in the matter, Victor Giwa, who appeared for himself, objected to the hearing of the motion and the continuation of the proceeding on the ground that he has presented a petition against the trial judge, alleging manifest bias, partisanship of the trial court.
Giwa alleged that the letter dated November 3 seeks the Chief Judge of FCT to investigate the allegation of bias and the disclosure of his private information to one of the complainants.
Giwa further stated that the court is highly partial in its proceeding and cannot get justice in the court.
He alleged that after the court requested for the phone number of his spouse, his spouse started receiving threat messages on her phone number.
The counsel to Chief Awa Kalu, in his argument in support of Giwa’s submission, urged the court to remit the file to the Chief Judge in light of the weighty allegations presented by Victor Giwa to the Court.
After Giwa’s application, the court ruled that it has not received any response to Giwa’s letter for recusal and ordered that the court will continue to hear the case. The proceeding was further adjourned to December 2, for ruling on Awa Kalu’s motion to set aside the subpoena .
